title: Commitment ladder + graduated overage bands and enterprise SQQ runbook
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Problem: Renewals conversations are stalling on two fronts: 1) Sales needs a defensible, repeatable framework to handle up-front committed discounts vs. observed expansion during a contract term; 2) Enterprise customers are asking for a streamlined security questionnaire + contract addendum process tied to renewals which is slowing close and causing legal rework.

Goal: Propose a pragmatic pricing and contract process that (a) gives Sales clear uplift/overage bands to offer at renewal and expansion, (b) introduces a simple multi-year commitment ladder for predictable discounts, and (c) pairs a lightweight SQQ runbook + modular contract addendum so Security/Legal reviews are predictable and fast.

Key components proposed: 
1) Commitment ladder (multi-year discounts):
   - 12-month commit: baseline list discount (example: 8% off list for committed spend >= $100k ARR)
   - 24-month commit: additional 6% (net ~14% off list, subject to minimal annual true-up floor)
   - 36-month commit: additional 9% (net ~21% off list)
   - All discounts conditional on a committed usage floor defined at signature. Discounts are applied only to committed quantity; non-committed usage billed at standard overage rules.

2) Graduated overage / uplift bands (applies during contract term):
   - Quarterly true-up cadence by default (option for monthly true-up for strategic customers).
   - Band A: usage up to 10% above committed quantity — no penalty, charged at committed unit price (automatic allowance to avoid micromanaging small growth).
   - Band B: 10% to 30% over committed quantity — charged at committed unit price + uplift multiplier (recommended +50% per-unit uplift above committed price).
   - Band C: >30% above committed quantity — charged at list rate or negotiated overage rate; Sales should re-engage for capacity/resizing conversation.
   - If sustained overage (two consecutive quarters in Band C), trigger a recommended amendment: increase commit or convert to Dedicated pricing.

3) Expansion credits / step-up provisions:
   - If a customer elects to increase committed quantity mid-term, apply pro-rated discount consistent with their ladder step. E.g., moving from 12->24 months takes effect immediately for the pro-rated portion.

4) SQQ (security questionnaire) runbook and modular contract addendum:
   - Runbook: sales sends SQQ intake form (one page) to Security; Security triages to Standard / Elevated / Executive review lanes with SLA targets (Standard: 3 business days; Elevated: 10 business days; Executive: 20 business days).
   - Standard lane covers typical infra, encryption-at-rest, TLS, RBAC, basic logging — handled by the pre-approved Fact Sheet + SOC2 excerpt.
   - Elevated lane adds KMS integration details, tenant isolation, custom logging retention. Requires Solutions Eng scoping call (30-60m).
   - Executive lane includes on-prem or air-gapped packaging, HSM integration, or contractual audit rights — handed to Legal + Security for negotiation.
   - Contract addendum template (modular): a set of short clauses the customer can opt into (KMS clause, data residency clause, audit clause, support SLA uplift). These clauses have pre-approved fallback language to avoid case-by-case redlines.

5) Operational and measurability hooks:
   - Sales playbook with script and examples for quoting uplift bands and multi-year ladder.
   - Billing triggers for quarterly true-ups and automated notices when a trailing 2-quarter usage average crosses Band B or C thresholds.
   - Dashboard for renewals leads showing customers in Band B/C and recommended outreach cadence.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Legal approves modular addendum language and pre-approved fallback text.
- Security signs off on runbook lanes and SLA targets.
- Sales pilot with 8 AE/AMs completes 10 renewal quotes using the ladder and uplift bands.
- Billing systems can produce quarterly usage reports and automated notices for pilot cohort.

Risks and trade-offs: 
- Too many micro-bands increases quote friction; solution: keep to three bands and clear examples.
- Deep discounting on long-term commits may reduce flexibility; mitigate with floors and clause that discounts apply only to committed quantity.
- SQQ lane misclassification could delay renewals; mitigate with intake form and strict SLA.

Next steps:

- Security to validate SQQ runbook lanes and provide the Standard Fact Sheet by 2026-03-20 — owner: Security (Eira Novak).
- Engineering/Billing to confirm feasibility of quarterly true-up notifications and report export by 2026-03-27 — owner: ENG billing team (owner TBD).
- Prepare pilot materials (template amendment, quoting sheet, AE playbook) by 2026-03-31.
